meaning: Verify Workflow interoperability with its original materialization and forward Operation providers, preserving source occurrences, selected recovery, uncertainty and captured identity.
inputs: Registered source graph, reconciled plan and complete boundary with exact source/certificate/plan identity; existing checked Workflow and Operation bindings and pinned definition bytes.

relations: Workflow occurrence calls its declared Operation
forward arguments refer to original materialization return
settled original Operation value feeds captured result
selected recovery plan orders binding preparation
exclusions: unique imported Operation is not one execution occurrence
compensation binding is not compensation execution
type-only reexport is not a runtime call
static closure is not interoperability proof

source_surface.roles: Workflow owns application/workflows wrapper, provider and materialization modules. Own paths, exports and imports derive from checked source/configuration. Materialization has no imports. Wrapper imports execute and reexports exactly WorkflowInput, WorkflowIdentity, WorkflowDependencies and WorkflowOutcome as types.
source_surface.provider_imports: Exact node:crypto createHash; namespace material import; type-only WorkflowInput reexport and import; uniquely sorted source forward Operation imports. Namespace runtime members are capture, captureResult, steps, result and compensations only when source compensations exist.
source_surface.closure: Merge independently derived Operation surfaces only for original forward targets. Repeated forward occurrences retain order; compensation-only and unrelated Operations remain outside this closure. Preserve complete boundary denominator and all source Workflow rows.
source_surface.registration: Weak-register exact surface; reject clone, foreign graph/plan/boundary and definition drift. Surface-ready never implies behavioral/native/currentness pass.

protocol.direct_scope: Direct Workflow calls into original materialization and forward Operations. Transitive Rule, Event and owned-value interactions remain separate Operation/factory families, not counted twice.
protocol.order: Validate execution identities; capture original workflow input once; check exact original Operation descriptors and capture selector-bound dependency objects before awaits; for each source occurrence materialize arguments, await its original Operation, inspect settlement and capture a committed result; finish with result materialization or selected recovery binding preparation.
protocol.identity: Preserve original wrapper/execute and forward Operation wrapper/provider identities. Arguments passed to each Operation must be the original materialization return; captureResult uses original captured input and original committed value; all following materialization calls use the same captured input and source-ordered original captured-result prefix. Preserve dependency identity by Operation selector. Track identity across cases, not only equal fields.
protocol.outcomes: Reuse complete finite Workflow cases and independent Workflow/Operation references. Preserve await traces, generated/required Event clocks, failed/uncertain commits, local materialization failure, recovery identities and dependency-constrained/reverse-completion tie breaking. No automatic compensation, retry, new transaction or implicit recovery effect.
protocol.observation: Record direct provider/member/occurrence, ordered calls and await settlement, exact arity, inert argument/return views, original identity links and input descriptor stability. Match complete final fixture observations independently. Native payload contains no expected answers.
protocol.capacity: All source Workflows retained. Missing complete success witness, resource exhaustion or unsupported complete family yields not_evaluable, never a passing prefix or a scalar substitute for compound cases.

audit: Dedicated source/native import-export module audit plus existing exact Workflow effect and whole-statement orchestration audits. Named createHash allowed only in the Workflow provider and only through the pinned metadata digest helper checked by the existing effect audit. Preserve source/native wrapper reexports, static namespace member closure and exact pinned Enum support. Do not weaken older Operation/factory audits.
execution: After original direct-call observation exists, use retained private execution with both audit phases, original modules and complete artifact/options/Node/TypeScript/platform currentness before, during and after execution. Reject cloned, stale, unavailable and incomplete evidence.
acceptance: Source-derived roles, export kinds and ordered import occurrences for all Workflow rows
Both layout roots, repeated forward Operation calls and no-compensation case
Real nested Entity/VO/Enum/sum/Event model, not fabricated scalar replacements
Dedicated source/native module, effect and orchestration audits reject compiling escapes
Original direct-call/identity checks reject missing, duplicate, wrong-provider and stale-captured-value calls even when final fields match
Retained artifact/tool currentness, no-prefix unavailable behavior and previous-family compatibility
claim_ceiling: Finite private instrumented Workflow interoperability only after original calls, all audits and retained custody pass. Surface/audit checkpoints alone do not complete ae12. No public aggregation, language/default change, release, admission, production compensation or authority.
native_format: Workflow interoperability follows the existing public Workflow verifier: strict ES2022 NodeNext ES-module output, with a module package boundary. Its native import/export checks and existing effect/orchestration facets inspect those original ESM modules. A future original-call observer must link original modules and preserve captured/export identities; do not infer CommonJS compatibility from ESM evidence.
